output.review_comment:
The first two fixes look reasonable: counting started periods with `(days_late + PERIOD_DAYS - 1) // PERIOD_DAYS` and rounding half-up with `+ 5000`. I'd merge them if they match the docstring.

The cap-vs-minimum change is the problem, and the PR description says so itself. The docstring says the one-fifth cap is applied after the minimum and that "the cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The new code only applies the cap when the raw percentage fee is above it. Otherwise it returns `max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS)`, which can be above the cap. For example, `late_fee_cents(1800, 45)` now returns 500 when the cap is 360. That breaks the docstring's rule. The code comment "Cap wins when fee exceeds it (even if cap < minimum)" is also misleading, because when the minimum is larger than the cap, the minimum wins.

The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth, and this logic was added only to make `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` pass. It fits the code to a test that looks wrong, which amounts to a quiet change to the fee policy for small balances. Please keep the docstring behavior, `min(max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS), balance_cents // 5)`. Then send the conflicting test (it expects 500, but the docstring gives 360) to the teammate or the test owner to decide. Don't change the test or the docstring yourself. Leaving that one test failing, with the conflict clearly explained, is better than shipping code that breaks the documented rule.
